title: Microvolume Spectrophotometer (Nucleic Acid Quantification)

references.label: General molecular biology laboratory manuals (ASM curriculum resources)

purpose: Measures the concentration and purity of nucleic acid (DNA/RNA) or protein samples using only 1-2 microliters, without a cuvette, by holding a small liquid column directly between two fiber-optic measurement surfaces.
operatingPrinciple: A small droplet of sample is pipetted onto the lower measurement pedestal, and the upper arm is lowered to form a liquid column of a fixed, very short path length held by surface tension; light is passed through this column and the resulting absorbance spectrum is used to calculate concentration (commonly via absorbance at 260 nm for nucleic acids) and purity ratios (e.g. A260/A280, A260/A230).
basicOperation: Clean both the upper and lower measurement surfaces before use, typically with a lint-free wipe and water.
Perform a blank measurement using the same buffer the sample is diluted/eluted in.
Pipette the small sample volume directly onto the lower pedestal and lower the upper arm to form the measurement column.
Initiate the measurement and record concentration and purity ratios.
Clean both surfaces again immediately after each sample to prevent carryover into the next measurement.
importantSettings: Correct blank/buffer selection (mismatched blank skews both concentration and purity ratio results)
Sample type setting (DNA vs. RNA vs. protein, which changes the wavelength/extinction coefficient used)
calibration: Periodic verification against a certified reference standard per manufacturer schedule.
maintenance: Clean both measurement surfaces after every single sample — residue from one sample can contaminate the next reading.
Avoid letting samples dry on the pedestal, which can leave residue affecting subsequent readings.

commonErrors.problem: Unexpectedly low or negative-looking A260/A280 or A260/A230 ratios
commonErrors.cause: Residual contaminant carryover from a previous sample (surfaces not cleaned), or a mismatched/incorrect blank
commonErrors.fix: Clean pedestals thoroughly between every sample and re-blank with the correct buffer

commonErrors.problem: Inconsistent concentration readings on repeat measurement of the same sample
commonErrors.cause: Air bubble in the sample column, or an unevenly mixed sample
commonErrors.fix: Mix the sample well before pipetting and re-load a fresh droplet, checking for bubbles

safety: Handle any biological/nucleic acid sample per its risk assessment.
